subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Lærdal Tunnel
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Lærdal Tunnel.

hook.text: Norway's Lærdal Tunnel is the world's longest road tunnel at 15.2 miles. Driving through takes 20 minutes.

buildup.text: To prevent driver fatigue and claustrophobia, the tunnel has three large illuminated caverns spaced evenly.

discovery.text: Blue and yellow lights in the caverns simulate sunrise, breaking up the monotonous darkness.

twist.text: Air quality is maintained by giant fans and an air treatment plant that scrubs exhaust continuously.

climax.text: The tunnel replaced a mountain pass that was closed in winter, linking communities year-round.

punchline.text: A tunnel with fake sunrises to keep drivers awake.

quiz.question: How does the Lærdal Tunnel combat driver fatigue?
options: Three illuminated caverns with colored lights simulating sunrise
